title: Improve quantized kernels: INT8/FP8 slow-path elimination and smoothquant+dequant fusion
author: Maya Chen
description:
Motivation: Recent customer workloads and internal perf tests showed a persistent slow-path when running INT8/FP8 quantized models. The slow-path is caused by separate smoothquant (per-channel scaling) and dequantization stages that materialize intermediate FP32/FP16 buffers and force non-coalesced GEMM kernels. This PR fuses smoothquant + dequant into the quantized GEMM execution path, and additionally removes a fallback slow-path for mixed INT8/FP8 kernels by adding specialized kernels and a light-weight dispatcher.

What this change does (high level):
- Fuse smoothquant scaling and the dequantization step directly into the quantized GEMM kernel pipeline, avoiding materialization of intermediate tensors.
- Add specialized kernels for common INT8/FP8 layouts (NCHW-like attention matmuls and dense feedforward matmuls). These kernels include fast-paths for: per-channel smoothquant scale application, FP8->FP16 accumulation variants, and a fused dequant+transpose when needed.
- Extend the runtime dispatcher to pick the new kernels when model metadata indicates compatible quantization params (scale tensor presence, block sizes). Falls back to existing kernels only when unsupported.
- Improve continuous batching and scheduler grouping heuristics to group requests by quantized format (INT8 vs FP8) to avoid mixing that forced slow-paths and deoptimized memory layouts.
- KV cache layout tweak: change cache tile ordering for quantized keys/values so kernels see coalesced memory in the fused path. Minimal memory layout migration logic included to preserve backward compatibility.

Benchmarks (internal):
- A100 (80GB) decoder-only 7B quantized model: p95 latency improved 18-23% and throughput +30% under steady batching.
- RTX 6000: p95 latency improved 15-20% and throughput +24%.
- Microbenchmarks show reduced DRAM traffic for quantized matmuls (~22% lower memory bytes moved) due to avoided materialization.

Compatibility and safety:
- The dispatcher performs a metadata compatibility check; if any tensor/scale layout is unsupported, we fall back to existing code paths. No operator ABI changes.
- Added unit tests and end-to-end perf test harness to prevent regressions.

Follow-ups:
- ENG-9123: extend FP8 wide-block kernels to support sequence-length > 2048 performance tuning.
- Add a small migration job that can detect older model artifacts and rewrite quant metadata to prefer the new fused path where safe.

Notes for reviewers: check the perf bench script in tests/perf for reproducibility steps, and the scheduler changes for potential regression on non-quantized workloads.

Small illustrative snippet (pseudo):
- Old: dequantize(x_scale, x_q) -> x_fp16; smoothquant_apply(x_fp16, alpha) -> x_scaled; gemm(x_scaled, w_fp16)->acc
- New fused flow inside kernel: for block in blocks: load_q = load_q_bytes(); scale = load_scale(); accum = fused_dequant_smoothquant_gemm(load_q, w_fp16, scale)

This description is intentionally detailed to aid reviewers in validating the performance improvements and correctness.
